correctness.rationale: Applying the binary recurrence to each fixed prefix, the middle zero block of length t=ell-8 and the reversed suffix gives ell, 4ell-12, 9ell-42 and 16ell-104. All four are canonical palindromes, including t=0. Subtracting multiples of ell gives a common divisor of ell and gcd(12,42,104)=2. The residue indicator of nonzero modulo three satisfies the Stern recurrence modulo two, so every even-length palindrome has even Stern value: mirrored digits cancel since 2=-1 modulo three. This gives the matching lower bound at even lengths. The short-length table exhausts the choices of a leading-one half word. Independent recurrence enumeration matched every short value and all gcds over 8190 canonical palindromes of lengths 1–24, plus 484 witness values for lengths 8–128. The four witnesses and parity argument, not the finite replay, prove the unrestricted law.

evidence: Theorem 1.1 gives a digit-pattern formula for individual Stern values. The Christoffel-word result in §9 addresses a full level. Record 0a25efd8bf3c gives exact ternary residue laws and lifts for the indices of even-length binary palindromes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A whole-layer distribution does not determine a restricted-layer gcd. The ternary-lift theorem is stronger on index residues, not on Stern value divisibility. Even combined with Stern parity it supplies a lower bound at even lengths, not sharpness or the odd-length law.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the exact gcd on the reversal-fixed set in each canonical binary layer, including the three exceptions to gcd(ell,2). The ingredients of binary transfer and the even-length divisibility obstruction are not new; the strongest inspected comparisons do not give the uniform upper bound or the fixed-length classification.
residual_risks: The targeted comparisons with existing Stern identities, tables and catalogue records do not exclude unindexed equivalent work under continuant or word formulations. This is not a claim of publication priority.

value.rationale: Canonical binary palindromes are precisely the fixed points of a natural symmetry of Stern values. A gcd across a whole fixed-length layer detects exactly its common arithmetic obstructions, rather than a chosen pair or numerical sample. The classification separates the forced factor two from all additional length-specific factors and supplies a uniform bounded-size witness for sharpness. This gives a reusable test of common divisibility in these layers without computing exponentially many values.
